subject: Post-meeting recap: inference unit economics & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Emily Turner <emily@brightguide.com>
Cc: Rohan Mehta <rohan@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-meeting recap: inference unit economics & next steps

Hi Emily — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap so we’re all aligned and to surface the next steps we agreed on. I kept this focused on the cost/throughput pain you emphasized.

Summary of pain points you shared
- Token/unit economics are a major cost pressure: currently pay-per-token hosted endpoints are accounting for >45% of model budget.
- Peak spikes (marketing campaigns + peaks from interactive product) drive large charges and unpredictable spend.
- Small batch sizes today due to a strict 150–200ms interactive latency target, so you don’t get batching/caching benefits.
- Concern about model quality regressions if quantization or larger batching is applied without validation.

Current stack (as discussed)
- Primary inference today: Open-hosted API (pay-per-token) for generation; lightweight local preprocessor for prompt templating.
- Serving layer sits on 2x A100-class GPUs per service cluster (self-managed).
- No prefix/KV caching in place; ephemeral session state stored in Redis.

Success criteria you called out (helpful for a trial)
- Reduce per-token cost by ~30% (measured in $/1k tokens).
- Maintain 95th percentile latency <= 200ms for interactive flows.
- No more than 1% top-level quality degradation on your customer-facing prompts (you’ll provide representative prompt set).
- Demonstrate at least 2x effective throughput on the same GPU footprint for batched workloads.

What Redwood can bring to the table (high level)
- Batching + dynamic scheduling to increase effective throughput while honoring latency SLOs.
- Automatic prefix/KV caching to cut redundant token work for common templates.
- Quantization options (4-bit/8-bit) with evaluation harness and rollback policies so you can validate quality quickly.
- Cost projection worksheet and sample config we can run against your traffic to estimate unit economics.

Immediate next steps (agreed on call)
1) You to share: a) representative prompt set and traffic profile (qps, peak shapes) b) example SLOs and any compliance gating notes — target by Wed 3/4.
2) Redwood deep-dive with Rohan (solutions eng) — 60–75m technical session to go over traffic shapes, perf counters and potential config knobs. Proposed slots: Thu 3/5 or Fri 3/6.
3) Procurement: we’ll send a cost worksheet + basic terms for a 4-week technical POC (no commitment) — initial doc attached.
4) If the POC looks good: discuss Dedicated/reserved pool sizing and a 3–6 month pilot.

Attachments: redwood-pricing-100k.pdf (sample cost worksheet), poc-outline-4week.docx (POC scope)

If I missed anything or misstated something, flag it and I’ll correct. Otherwise I’ll wait for the prompt set and traffic profile and will book the technical deep-dive once you confirm availability.

Thanks again — excited to help BrightGuide tighten up inference economics.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0172

From: Emily Turner <emily@brightguide.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightguide.com
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-meeting recap: inference unit economics & next steps

Marissa — thanks for the clear write-up. This matches our notes; a few clarifications from my side:

1) Stack details
- We currently use hosted generation for our conversational flows (pay-per-token). Model delta experiments run on a small internal cluster (2 A100s per service) for private evaluations.
- Our prompting patterns are fairly templated which is why caching sounds promising.

2) Latency and batching
- Our tolerance for interactive UX is 150–200ms 95th. Most callers are sensitive — anything above that shows as churn in our metrics. We’d prefer to keep headroom.
- We don’t have batching in production — teams are worried about latency jitter.

3) Quantization/regulatory
- We are open to quantization but need a formal validation step. Legal will push back if we can’t prove parity. Happy to run the Redwood harness you mentioned.

4) Procurement asks
- Please send the cost worksheet and the basic POC terms (scope, data handling, SSO requirements). Our procurement lead copied here will need those to spin up a PO.

Next small ask: can you double-check whether Redwood can simulate our traffic shape given short bursty peaks? If yes, please outline what telemetry/data you’d need and we’ll prioritize sending that with the prompt set.

I’ll aim to get the prompt set + traffic profile to you by EOD Wed 3/4. Procurement: procurement@brightguide.com — they’ll expect the worksheet and a short terms summary.

Thanks — Emily
Emily Turner
Head of Product Engineering
BrightGuide
emily@brightguide.com | +1 (212) 555-6410
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Emily Turner <emily@brightguide.com>
Cc: Rohan Mehta <rohan@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Mar 2026 09:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-meeting recap: inference unit economics & next steps

Emily — perfect, thanks for the confirmations. Quick logistics and concrete asks so we can move the POC forward:

What we need from BrightGuide (by EOD Wed 3/4 if possible)
- Representative prompt set (10–20 prompts across interactive + long-form generation), anonymized if needed.
- Traffic profile: steady-state qps, peak qps, peak duration, percent interactive vs batch. CSV or simple JSON is fine.
- Any legal/compliance flags (e.g., cannot persist prompts beyond eval window).

What Redwood will deliver for the 4-week POC
- Configuration: batching + caching profiles tuned for your latency SLOs; quantization trials (4-bit & 8-bit) on a copy of your prompt set with our evaluation harness.
- Metrics: $/1k tokens projection, 95th latency, throughput improvement, and top-1 quality delta for the provided prompts.
- Weekly checkpoint calls and final findings deck.

Proposed kickoff timeline
- Thu 3/5 or Fri 3/6: 60–75m technical deep-dive with Rohan (solutions) and your engineering lead — please confirm preferred slot.
- Week of 3/9: POC runs start once we have the prompt set + traffic profile and a brief security checklist.

I’ll attach the cost worksheet and POC scope (attached). I’ll also drop a calendar invite for both Thu 3/5 10:00am PT and Fri 3/6 11:00am PT; feel free to accept either and we’ll remove the other.

If procurement needs anything else for a PO we can produce a short SOW after the technical kickoff.

Thanks again — we’ll be ready to simulate bursty peaks; Rohan will request the traffic bins (minute-level) and any historical billing snapshots needed for an accurate unit-econ projection.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
